briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East remains a high-tension flashpoint with intense diplomatic activity surrounding potential US-Iran talks in Pakistan, despite contradictions on direct engagement. Meanwhile, Israel and Hezbollah continue cross-border exchanges, including Israeli strikes in Lebanon and Hezbollah drone operations, signaling persistent conflict. The US has significantly increased its military presence in the region by deploying three aircraft carrier groups simultaneously, while simultaneously enacting new sanctions on Iranian oil trade networks.

IRAN
Diplomatic efforts are underway in Pakistan involving Iran and the United States, facilitated by Pakistani mediators. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi is in Islamabad for bilateral consultations with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Asim Munir, stating that Iran's positions and "observations" will be conveyed to the US via Pakistan. Conversely, the White House claims Iran initiated contact requesting direct talks and is sending US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Islamabad, with President Trump suggesting Iran will present an offer to meet American demands. Iranian state media outlet Tasnim and the Foreign Ministry spokesman vehemently deny any planned direct meetings, calling White House claims false and asserting Iran has rejected US negotiation requests. There are conflicting reports regarding Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf's resignation as head of the negotiation team; Iran International and Axios reported his stepping down due to infighting, while Iran's Parliament Communications Bureau denies it. Araghchi's regional tour also includes Oman and Russia.

Militarily, Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned the US military of a "decisive response" if it persists in "blockade, piracy, and maritime robbery" in the region, emphasizing Iran's readiness and control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz. The Defense Ministry stated that a "significant portion" of Iran’s missile capabilities remains unused and that the armed forces maintained "full control over the skies of the occupied territories" until the ceasefire. The IRGC seized a ship suspected of cooperation with the US military, which it claims had made several trips to US ports in the past six months. President Pezeshkian invoked the "historic defeat" of the US in Tabas and a "new Tabas" in southern Isfahan. Reports of controlled explosions in Dezful and Isfahan are due to the demolition of unexploded ordnance.

Internally, Iran executed an individual accused of being an "agent working for Israel" and sabotage during January protests. Erfan Kiani, one of the December 2025 protestors, was executed in Isfahan. Death sentences for three citizens, Ehsan Hosseinipour Hesarlou, Matin Mohammadi, and Erfan Amiri (17 and 18 years old), related to the Pakdasht mosque arson and murder, have been upheld by the Supreme Court. The internet remains cut in Iran for over 1320 hours (56 days), which NetBlocks reports as the longest recorded global shutdown. Iranian officials justify this by "not being expedient" to restore it. International flights have resumed from Imam Khomeini International Airport, and Tabriz airport, which sustained damage at 12 points during US-Zionist attacks, is expected to reopen within a week. The government has extended the deadline for returning foreign currency to June 9, 2026. President Pezeshkian has called on citizens to reduce electricity and energy consumption, citing concerns about enemy efforts to create dissatisfaction.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces continue military operations in the region. In southern Lebanon, the IDF intercepted a "suspicious aerial target," suspected to be a Hezbollah drone, before it crossed into Israeli territory. The Israeli Air Force struck Hezbollah rocket launchers overnight in Deir ez-Zahrani, Kfar Reman, and Sammaaiyeh, and later in Yater and Kafra, stating these posed a "real threat" to IDF troops and Israeli civilians. In Bint Jbeil, troops from the Paratroopers Brigade killed six armed Hezbollah gunmen in an exchange of fire; two were killed by soldiers and four in an airstrike on their building. An Oketz canine unit dog was killed during this operation. The IDF also struck military buildings in Deir Aames, from which rockets were launched at Shtula, warning residents to evacuate prior to the strikes.

In the Gaza Strip, the IDF struck and killed armed Palestinian terror operatives in a pickup truck in the south who were planning "imminent" attacks, and eliminated armed Hamas operatives in the north who posed a threat to nearby Israeli forces.

On the home front, Nessia Kradi, an 11-year-old girl from Bnei Brak, died from injuries sustained in an Iranian missile attack. Israeli forces, in cooperation with police, foiled an attempt to smuggle 12 handguns from Jordan using a drone, arresting one smuggler. Two kites from Gaza were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz and are under investigation. Near Jenin refugee camp, 20 unarmed suspects were identified, with most apprehended by IDF and Border Police. An investigation has been launched into an attempted breach of a High Court hearing regarding the October 7 inquiry. Prime Minister Netanyahu stated he had an "excellent conversation" with President Trump, discussing close cooperation on Iranian pressure. Netanyahu affirmed Israel's "complete freedom of action" against Hezbollah, confirming strikes "yesterday and today," with a determination to restore security to northern residents.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, Israeli forces conducted airstrikes, eliminating armed Palestinian terror operatives in the south who were "working to advance imminent terror plots" against IDF forces. Further strikes targeted armed Hamas operatives in the north who "posed a threat" to Israeli forces. The Hamas-run interior ministry in Gaza claimed the latter strike targeted their police force members, resulting in several killed and wounded. Kites from Gaza were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, prompting an IDF investigation. Palestinian Authority Chairman Mahmoud Abbas participated in local elections held in the West Bank and Gaza, including Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, where Hamas police were observed. Hamas and other Palestinian resistance groups have denounced Israeli assaults on Gaza as "full-fledged war crimes."

LEBANON
Cross-border hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah persist. Lebanese reports indicate four to six fatalities from an Israeli strike in Yohmor al-Shaqif, southern Lebanon. The IDF intercepted a suspicious aerial target over southern Lebanon, which did not cross into Israeli territory. Israeli forces also conducted overnight strikes on Hezbollah rocket launchers in Deir ez-Zahrani, Kfar Reman, and Sammaaiyeh, and later in Yater and Kafra. Six armed Hezbollah gunmen were killed in Bint Jbeil by Israeli paratroopers, supported by tank shelling and an explosive drone. The IDF also struck buildings in Deir Aames, after rockets were fired from there towards Shtula. Hezbollah claimed to have struck an Israeli army Humvee in Qantara with an explosive drone (footage for an April 22 strike), and the IDF reported Hezbollah launched several more explosive-laden drones on Israeli troops in southern Lebanon today, which the IDF called a "blatant violation of the ceasefire agreement." Hezbollah official Mahmoud Qamati declared that no regional or international power can force the movement to disarm. Indonesia condemned Israel for the killing of another Indonesian UNIFIL soldier.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, explosions were reported in Homs. Iraqi Kurdistan has reportedly suffered over 800 attacks since the start of the conflict. In Karbala, Iraq, an armed attack resulted in two casualties belonging to an offshoot organization connected to al-Sadr's movement, leading to the freezing of Saraya al-Salam (al-Sadr's movement) in the province. The Kuwaiti army reported two fiber-optic guided explosive drones, launched from Iraq, struck two locations in northern Kuwait, causing material damage but no injuries. US military aircraft, including F-35s and C-17s, were observed flying over Anbar province (Al-Rutbah) and Mosul in Iraq. Nejaf International Airport announced the resumption of Meraj Airlines flights to Tehran and Mashhad.

GULF STATES
Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad discussed the US-Iran ceasefire agreement with President Trump, with Qatar affirming its support for Pakistan's mediation efforts. Saudi Arabia issued a statement rejecting violations of state sovereignty and threats to regional security, urging the Iraqi government to responsibly address threats to Gulf states. The US has expanded its military presence at Al Dhafra Air Base in the UAE, including fighter jets and KC-135R refuelers. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi's regional tour includes Oman, where Iran's ambassador states Oman remains a top regional friend. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius indicated Germany would dispatch a minelayer to the Mediterranean for potential deployment in the Strait of Hormuz, but only after the end of hostilities and with parliamentary approval. Two oil tankers, the Chinese-owned "Peace Gulf" and the Greek-owned "NJ Jupiter," passed through the Strait of Hormuz with Iranian permission. The Arab League Council, at the foreign minister level, condemned Iran's threats to obstruct navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, holding Iran responsible for any resulting damages and calling for UN Security Council intervention.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Intensified Diplomacy:** Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi is in Islamabad for bilateral talks with Pakistani officials, while the US is sending envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for indirect engagement, with the possibility of direct US-Iran talks if progress is made, despite Iran's public denial of direct negotiations.
2.  **Lebanon Escalation:** Six Hezbollah gunmen were killed by Israeli forces in Bint Jbeil, and Israel conducted airstrikes on Hezbollah rocket launchers across southern Lebanon, while Hezbollah launched explosive drones at Israeli troops, escalating cross-border exchanges.
3.  **US Military Buildup:** The United States has deployed three aircraft carrier strike groups (USS Abraham Lincoln, USS Gerald R. Ford, USS George H.W. Bush) simultaneously in the Middle East for the first time in decades, alongside other naval assets, indicating a significant military posture increase.
4.  **US Economic Pressure:** The Trump administration imposed new sanctions on a major Chinese refinery and 40 shipping companies linked to Iranian oil smuggling and ended oil trade waivers for Iran and Russia.
5.  **Internal Repression in Iran:** Iran executed an alleged Israeli agent, Erfan Kiani (a December 2025 protestor), and upheld death sentences for three minors (Ehsan Hosseinipour Hesarlou, Matin Mohammadi, Erfan Amiri) involved in the Pakdasht mosque arson. The nationwide internet shutdown persists for over 56 days.
6.  **Strait of Hormuz Warnings:** Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned the US against "maritime piracy" and "blockade" in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a "decisive response" if such actions continue, while Iran's Defense Ministry claimed firm control over the waterway.
7.  **Mali Conflict:** Jihadist groups affiliated with JNIM attacked and seized military positions and cities, including Kidal and Gao, in Mali, with some attacks targeting Russian Africa Corps forces, leading the US Embassy to advise citizens to shelter in place.
8.  **Child Casualty:** Nessia Kradi, an 11-year-old Israeli girl from Bnei Brak, succumbed to injuries sustained from an Iranian missile attack.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain critically high due to conflicting claims surrounding US-Iran negotiations, the intensified US military posture, and ongoing hostilities in Lebanon. Active flashpoints include the Israel-Lebanon border, where Israeli strikes and Hezbollah drone attacks persist despite an alleged ceasefire. The Strait of Hormuz is another critical flashpoint, with Iranian warnings against US maritime actions and US threats to engage "minelayers." The US military's deployment of three aircraft carrier groups for the first time in decades significantly raises the potential for direct confrontation. US Defense Secretary Hegseth's assertive rhetoric against Iran, combined with new sanctions, further elevates tensions. Iran's assertions of unused missile capabilities and firm control over the Strait of Hormuz suggest a preparedness for further conflict, which, if engaged, could lead to a broader regional confrontation. Internally, Iran faces continued unrest and repression, potentially creating further instability that could spill over.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**US Posture:** The US is pursuing a dual-track strategy of diplomacy and pressure. White House officials state that envoys Witkoff and Kushner are traveling to Pakistan for potential direct talks with Iran, while President Trump claims Iran is seeking a deal. Militarily, the US has significantly bolstered its presence in the Middle East with three aircraft carrier strike groups and other naval assets. Defense Secretary Hegseth maintained a hardline stance, asserting US control over the Strait of Hormuz, continuing a naval blockade, and warning Iran against "piracy," while also expanding federal death penalty options domestically. Economically, new sanctions target a Chinese refinery and 40 shipping companies for involvement in Iranian oil, and waivers for oil trade with Iran and Russia have been terminated. The State Department's legal counsel considers the "Iran war" a continuation of conflict since 1979, aiming to circumvent congressional approval deadlines.

**Gulf States:** Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad discussed the ceasefire with President Trump, endorsing Pakistan's mediation. Saudi Arabia condemned violations of state sovereignty and threats to regional security, calling on Iraq to address threats emanating from its territory. The Arab League Foreign Ministers issued a joint statement condemning Iran's threats to obstruct navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, holding Iran responsible for any damages. Kuwait reported drone attacks on its northern territory originating from Iraq.

**EU Members:** Germany's Defense Minister Pistorius announced the deployment of a minelayer to the Mediterranean, prepared for potential post-war operations in the Strait of Hormuz, subject to parliamentary approval. Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged increased pressure on Iran, with potential sanction relief for compromise. French President Emmanuel Macron questioned the reliability of the United States as an ally. Air France has canceled flights to Dubai, Riyadh, Beirut, and Tel Aviv until May 18. Spain's Defense Minister Margarita Robles demanded respect for Spain's role in NATO, in response to reports of the Pentagon considering suspending Spain's NATO membership for not supporting the US war on Iran.

**Russia:** Russia is engaged in diplomatic discussions with Pakistan and Iran. Its Africa Corps forces were reportedly targeted by jihadist groups in Mali. Russia launched a major air attack on Ukraine, involving 619 drones and 47 missiles, leading to a drone crash in Romania. Initial reports of British NATO planes downing Russian drones over Romania were rejected by the UK Ministry of Defense.

**China:** China reportedly advised its citizens to leave Iran immediately. The US has imposed sanctions on a large Chinese refinery and numerous shipping companies for their involvement in smuggling Iranian oil.

**Turkey:** Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan stated that Turkey might consider participating in demining operations in the Strait of Hormuz following a potential US-Iran peace agreement.

**United Kingdom:** Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced plans to introduce legislation to proscribe the IRGC as a terrorist organization.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
**Contradictions and Unverified Claims:** A significant contradiction exists regarding the nature of US-Iran talks in Pakistan: the White House asserts Iran requested direct engagement, while Iranian officials emphatically deny this, stating communications will only be conveyed via Pakistani mediators. Reports of Parliament Speaker Qalibaf's resignation as lead negotiator are also contested, with some sources claiming it and others denying it. The alleged Chinese evacuation order for its citizens from Iran lacks official confirmation. Similarly, the status of Mojtaba Khamenei, reportedly severely injured, is presented as ongoing treatment by some Iranian sources, while an Israeli journalist suggests this could be Iranian disinformation. Unverified reports include a shooting incident in Malard, Iran, allegedly by a 15-year-old Basiji, and the presence of Iraqi Hashed al-Shaabi forces chanting against Iranians in Shiraz. Conflicting accounts of Russian drone interception by NATO forces over Romania were also observed.

**Propaganda Indicators:** Iranian state media frequently employs ideologically charged language, such as "aggressor US military," "Zionist enemies," and "historic defeat," to frame events and bolster domestic support. The White House's assertion that Iran initiated the request for direct talks may be a tactical move to project leverage. Conversely, anti-regime channels often use highly inflammatory language and circulate unverified claims, as seen in reports regarding internal Iranian incidents.

**Reporting Gaps:** Specific details regarding the precise demands and offers exchanged between Iran and the US through Pakistani mediation are not publicly disclosed. The exact identity and flag of the ship seized by the IRGC, beyond its suspected cooperation with the US military, remain unclear. The full extent of damage and specific objectives of jihadist groups in Mali beyond "overthrow the government" are not clearly articulated. Causalties reported for Israeli strikes in Lebanon varied between four and six, indicating a lack of precise verification.
